cross_cultural.criterion: level 1: demographic statistics only, a disclosure rather than an activity

cross_cultural.reason: Level 1. The 10-K offers equal-employment-opportunity boilerplate, a federal-contractor commitment to hire veterans and people with disabilities, and demographic percentages (E1). It describes no specific practice such as employee networks, accessibility programs, multilingual services or community-connecting programs. The supplied report text adds nothing on this theme. The relevant 10-K discussion is about 130 words, under the roughly 150-word threshold, so coverage stays insufficient.

ai.notes: The supplied 'report chapters' contain only the CEO letter from the Valero Report on Guiding Principles (2024 performance year). They cover safety, operations and low-carbon investment, and have no people, community, education or inclusion content, even though they were described as those chapters. The second look therefore could not use any relevant report material. A human should check whether the correct People/Community chapters were pulled. In the 10-K, the commitment to hire and retain veterans and individuals with disabilities is framed as a federal-contractor obligation ('we are committed to'), so it is commitment and compliance language, not a scorable activity. The 10-K also points to the 2025 Valero Report on Guiding Principles for community and employee disclosures. Because coverage is still insufficient, this company should go to team review before being ranked last.
